title: Common generic stalk isomorphism
statement: Let S and C be integral schemes and c:C → S a smooth morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let Cη be integral and let q:Cη → Spec K(S), j:Cη → C form a cartesian generic fibre [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there is e:Spec K(C) ≅ Spec K(Cη) with (e.hom ≫ Cη.fromSpecStalk(η_Cη)) ≫ j = C.fromSpecStalk(η_C). Normality and geometric connectedness are not needed for this assertion.

source.place: Tag 01UA; Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Stalk (fromSpecStalk preimmersion and naturality), Morphisms.Preimmersion (base change), and Limits (pullback range)

proof.text: The generic-stalk spectrum has dense image in S. The pullback range formula and openness of c show j has dense image. The image of a generic point under a dominant continuous map is generic, so j(η_Cη)=η_C.

The generic-stalk spectrum map is a preimmersion and preimmersions are stable under base change. Thus j is a preimmersion and its generic stalk map is surjective. After transporting along the generic-point equality, this is a homomorphism of fields, hence injective, and therefore an isomorphism. Take the inverse of its Spec isomorphism; stalk-map and stalk-specialization naturality give the required compatibility.

lean.statement:
theorem smooth_connected_generic_geometry_stalk_iso {S C : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral S]
    [IsIntegral C] (c : C ⟶ S) [Smooth c]
    {Cη : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Cη]
    (q : Cη ⟶ Spec S.functionField) (j : Cη ⟶ C)
    (hCη : IsPullback q j (S.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint S)) c) :
    ∃ e : Spec C.functionField ≅ Spec Cη.functionField,
      (e.hom ≫ Cη.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint Cη)) ≫ j =
        C.fromSpecStalk (genericPoint C)
